subject: mathematics
question_text: Define a skew symmetric matrix. If the matrix with rows (0, 2, 1), (−2, 0, −2) and (−1, x, 0) is skew symmetric, find the value of x.

recall_prompt: Say what a skew symmetric matrix is and how you would find x.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define skew symmetric
steps.margin_note: First mark. Skew symmetric means A = −Aᵀ — the SAME as symmetric but with a minus sign, which is also why every diagonal entry has to be 0.
lines: A square matrix A is skew symmetric if A = −Aᵀ.

recall.must_convey: That a square matrix is skew symmetric when it equals the NEGATIVE of its transpose, A = −Aᵀ.
accept: a square matrix is skew symmetric if it equals minus its transpose
skew symmetric means A equals negative A transpose
the matrix is the negative of its own transpose
skew symmetric ante A equals minus A transpose
transposing it and changing every sign gives back the same matrix

steps.why: Skew symmetry is symmetry with a sign flip. That flip also forces every diagonal entry to be zero, which the given matrix already satisfies — a useful check that the question is consistent.
common_mistakes: Defining it as A = Aᵀ, which is plain symmetric.

steps.label: Equate the mirror entries
steps.margin_note: Second mark. In −Aᵀ the (3,2) entry is −(the (2,3) entry of A) = −(−2) = 2. Setting that equal to x gives the answer.

recall.must_convey: That skew symmetry makes the (3,2) entry the negative of the (2,3) entry, so x = −(−2) = 2.
accept: the entry is minus the mirrored one so x equals minus of minus two which is two
skew symmetry gives x as the negative of the reflected entry so x is two
x equals minus negative two which is two

steps.why: Under skew symmetry mirrored entries are opposite in sign. Missing the sign flip gives x = −2, which is the wrong answer by exactly that flip.
common_mistakes: Writing x = −2 by treating it as symmetric.
